proposed.text: What is the primary purpose of specifying a uniformity ratio (UR) of 0.6 minimum in general occupied spaces per IES standards?

options.text: To ensure 60% of fixtures operate at rated capacity, optimizing energy efficiency and lighting performance
To guarantee average illumination across the space is at least 60% of peak illumination, providing consistent lighting conditions
To prevent dark zones by ensuring minimum illumination is at least 60% of average illumination
To limit energy consumption to 60% of the building's total lighting budget, promoting sustainable design practices

proposed.rationale: UR 0.6 means the darkest point must receive at least 60% of average illumination, preventing dark zones and reducing eye strain. This prevents excessive brightness variation across a space. [A]: Fixture capacity and operating levels are independent of uniformity ratio; UR addresses spatial consistency, not individual fixture output. [B]: This inverts the definition; UR compares minimum to average, not average to peak. Peak illumination (brightest points) may far exceed average. [D]: Uniformity ratio is a spatial quality metric, not an energy budget allocation; energy consumption is managed through lighting power density (LPD) limits.
proposed.code_citation: Article: Illumination Levels by Occupancy and Task, Section: Uniformity Ratio
